mechanism_narrative: A higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which is associated with lower corporate earnings growth and reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is linear and holds across all economic regimes.
failure_condition: The hypothesis fails if the correlation between UNRATE and 20-day forward returns is not negative (Pearson correlation < -0.1) or if the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 12-month increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.0% signals accelerating inflation, which triggers a sell-off in equities due to rising real interest rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The hypothesis fails if, in periods when CPIAUCSL 12m change > 3.0%, the 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) growth rate (3m change) declines and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises, it signals a deteriorating economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The joint condition of INDPRO decline and UNRATE rise is the trigger for the negative return signal.
failure_condition: The hypothesis fails if, in periods when INDPRO 3m change < 0 AND UNRATE 3m change > 0, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a severe economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal is active only when both conditions are met: FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and INDPRO 3m change < 0.
failure_condition: The hypothesis fails if, in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% AND INDPRO 3m change < 0, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A lower housing starts (HOUST) indicates weak demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is linear and holds across all economic regimes.
failure_condition: The hypothesis fails if the correlation between HOUST and 20-day forward returns is not negative (Pearson correlation < -0.1) or if the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production (INDPRO) growth rate (3m change) exceeds 2.5%, it signals robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is active when INDPRO 3m change > 2.5%.
failure_condition: The hypothesis fails if, in periods when INDPRO 3m change > 2.5%, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline and retail sales (RSAFS) also decline, it signals a weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The joint condition of HOUST decline and RSAFS decline is the trigger for the negative return signal.
failure_condition: The hypothesis fails if, in periods when HOUST 3m change < 0 AND RSAFS 3m change < 0, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) is offset by a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal is active only when both conditions are met: UNRATE < 3.5% and INDPRO 3m change < 0.
failure_condition: The hypothesis fails if, in periods when UNRATE < 3.5% AND INDPRO 3m change < 0, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
